experiment: E2: the head's share of a decode step on a small model, in the fastest Hugging Face configuration, and the step with the certified head by substitution
written: 2026-11-17, after E1, the head-share table, G1's addendum on Qwen3-0.6B and the unified kernel's A100 run were read, before any E2 code ran
why: E1 found the head to be 1% to 4% of a decode step on 8B-and-larger models in an eager Hugging Face loop, so no head speed-up could show. Qwen3-0.6B's output layer is 21% of its weights, and it sits at the byte floor untuned. A compiled body with a static cache removes most of the host overhead. This is the most favourable case we can measure with the tools at hand.
model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B at c1899de2, BF16, batch 1, 24 prompts (four per language group), greedy

measured.step_eager: milliseconds per new token of model.generate with the default cache: (time for 72 new tokens - time for 8) / 64, each prompt run once to warm up and once timed
measured.step_static: the same with cache_implementation = 'static', and again with model.forward compiled by torch.compile(mode = 'reduce-overhead'). Whichever is fastest is the step used below. Failures are recorded, not hidden.
measured.head_stock: the stock head alone on 512 saved greedy states of this model: BF16 product and argmax, graph-captured, CUDA events
measured.head_cert: the unified kernel (fused2.py, shift 0.5, no K2) on the same states, graph-captured; every token checked against the FP32 reference

derived: head share = head_stock / step; estimated certified step = step - head_stock + head_cert. This is an estimate by substitution: the certified head is not run inside generate.

prediction_written_before_running.tokens: no certified token differs from the reference
prediction_written_before_running.eager: in the eager loop the head is under 3% of a step on both GPUs
prediction_written_before_running.fastest: in the fastest configuration the head is 4% to 9% of a step on the A100 and 7% to 15% on the A10G
prediction_written_before_running.head_ratio: the certified head takes 0.60 to 0.85 of the stock head on the A100 and 0.40 to 0.75 on the A10G
prediction_written_before_running.end_to_end: the estimated certified step is 0.97 to 0.995 of the stock step on the A100 and 0.93 to 0.98 on the A10G. So even here the end-to-end gain is a few percent.
prediction_written_before_running.takeaway_if_wrong: If the head's share exceeds 20% in the fastest configuration, an end-to-end saving of 5% or more is within reach and a real integration (the certified head inside the compiled step) is worth building. If the compiled configurations fail, the eager number stands and the question stays open.
